projects.title: From draft to deploy.
projects.description: Things I built alone, with a team and out of pure curiosity. Open source whenever possible.

items.romulodm: This site: a highly over-engineered portfolio and blog, built to show what I've done and what I plan to do. Next.js up front, a queue worker and a search engine in Go, all on one VPS.
items.seedicon: An npm package that turns any string into a deterministic SVG avatar. 17 styles, zero dependencies, no image storage. It draws the avatars on this very site.
items.modernLiveMessenger: MSN Messenger rebuilt for the browser with two friends, in React on top of 7.css. Real-time chat, winks, the nudge that shakes the window, and ChatGPT as a contact.
items.goChess: Multiplayer chess for a course whose point was picking a language new to us. React draws the board, and Go keeps two-player rooms in sync over Gorilla WebSocket.
items.goBet: A toy casino built to study microservices: Go services for auth, email and roulette talking over gRPC, with JWT, queries generated by sqlc and a React front end.
items.interzap: A terminal WhatsApp on Python sockets, built for a Computer Networks course following the professor's protocol. Groups, read receipts, and SQLite holding messages for offline users.
items.pacMan: Pac-Man in Python, my first undergraduate project. The maze is a 28x31 matrix and each ghost chases in its own way, with A* plotting routes for the hunters.
items.eCommerce: A full storefront built to learn the stack the market wanted: React and Redux up front, Express and MySQL behind, with JWT login, a cart, an admin panel and password recovery.
items.game2048: 2048 in Python, made at a friend's suggestion. The whole game lives in a 4x4 matrix: compressing rows, merging tiles, checking for a win or a loss. The interface just draws it.

whoami.title: Life is not a mystery to be solved, but an experience to be lived.
whoami.paragraph1: I saw this quote in the movie Dune and thought a lot about it. I believe that many times we turn our insignificance into a form of martyrdom and doubt, when in reality things should be simpler than they actually are.
whoami.paragraph2: You and I are not mere candidates for a place in heaven. If you always live thinking about a future reward, you end up forgetting to live in the present and forgetting who you are.
whoami.paragraph3: According to Jean-Paul Sartre, existence precedes essence. This means that human beings have no predetermined nature. You create your own nature through your actions and choices. Therefore, this question has no correct answer. The responsibilities you take on and the choices you make throughout your life determine who you are.
whoami.paragraph4: Today you might be a programmer, a student, a professional... However, tomorrow you might be a completely different person — it all depends on you.

about.title: About this site
about.description: I believe that building in public is the best way to grow. I created this portfolio and blog to share ideas, projects, and lessons learned along the journey.
about.community: If you're here, you're already part of this community.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: The basics about this place, in a few lines.

items.a: It's my portfolio and my blog in one place. On one side, what I've built and the stack I work with; on the other, writing about engineering, infrastructure and the decisions behind the projects — including the mistakes, which usually teach more than the wins.

items.q: Do I have to pay for anything?
items.a: No. Everything here is free: no paywall, no reading limit, no ads. You don't even need an account to read.

Sharing a post with someone who'd enjoy it already helps a lot. If you'd like to support it financially, you can buy me a coffee via PIX, card or crypto — it covers hosting and the time spent writing. Pointing out a mistake in a post counts for a lot too.

items.q: What do I get by subscribing to the newsletter?
items.a: An email when a new post goes out, and nothing else. No spam, no list selling, no marketing blasts. The unsubscribe link is in every message and works in one click.
An open space for anyone passing by to leave a short note. No theme and no rules beyond common sense: a hello, a topic suggestion, or just marking that you were here.

items.q: Do I need an account to comment?
items.a: Not to read. To comment or like, yes — signing in with Google, GitHub, or email and password. The account only exists to keep spam out and the conversation accountable; I don't use your data for anything else.
It is. The whole site, the infrastructure and the workers are public on GitHub. If you want to understand how a piece of it works, or reuse something, just browse the repository.

cookieBanner.title: Allow cookies?
cookieBanner.description: Google Analytics is always on. "Allow" adds demographics.

whatAreCookies.title: What are cookies?
whatAreCookies.body: Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit a website. They are widely used to make websites work more efficiently and to provide information to site owners.

essential.title: 1. Essential cookies
essential.body: Always on. They include session and security cookies, the cookie that stores your banner choice and the Google Analytics 4 cookies (_ga and _ga_*), used to measure in aggregate which pages are visited, where traffic comes from and how people navigate. Measurement relies on legitimate interest (LGPD, art. 7, IX) and is not used for advertising.

performance.title: 2. Audience metrics
performance.body: Google Analytics 4 records page views, scrolling, outbound link clicks, searches, downloads and form and video interactions, together with technical data such as browser, device and approximate location (city). Google does not log or store the full IP address. The data is processed by Google in the United States.

functionality.title: 3. Functionality cookies
functionality.body: They let the site remember your choices, such as language and theme. They stay in your browser and do not track your browsing on other sites.

targeting.title: 4. Google signals (optional)
targeting.body: Only enabled when you click "Allow". With them, Google associates visits from people signed in to a Google account to produce aggregated reports on age, gender, interests and cross-device use. No data is used to personalize ads. With "Essential only", signals stay off.

manage.title: 5. How to manage or object
manage.body: To turn Google Analytics off in this browser, use the link in section 7.4 of the <link>Privacy Policy</link>. To change your banner choice, delete the cookie_consent cookie and the banner shows again. You can also block cookies in your browser settings.
